subject: Energy
title: Liquid Air Energy Storage
description: Learn Liquid Air Energy Storage in one minute.

hook.text: LAES cools air to −196°C until it liquefies—storing it in insulated tanks for later expansion through a turbine.

buildup.text: Surplus electricity powers the cooling—liquid air shrinks to 1/700th the volume of gas, making storage compact.

discovery.text: When power is needed, liquid air is heated, expands 700x, and drives a turbine—clean, with no combustion.

twist.text: Waste heat from nearby industrial sites can boost efficiency—coupling LAES with factories creates symbiotic benefits.

climax.text: Highview Power built a 50 MW / 250 MWh LAES plant in the UK—proving the concept at commercial scale.

punchline.text: Freeze the air, then let it expand—cold storage, hot power.
